item.title: For no real reason, I decided to look at the frequency of gaps…
item.dc:creator: @robpike.io
item.description:
For no real reason, I decided to look at the frequency of gaps between the prime numbers: 1 between 2 and 3, 2 between 3 and 5, 2 again between 5 and 7, and so on. The results are noisier than I expected. Pretty consistently up to hundreds of millions, the most frequent gap by a large margin is 6, first appearing between 23 and 29.

The ivy code:

op gaps n =
p = primes n
gaps = (1 drop p) - -1 drop p
u = u[up u = unique gaps]
transp (2, (rho u)) rho u, (+/%@ u @== gaps)

item.title: Running MacOS 27.0.1. I usually wait for the .1 release but was…
item.dc:creator: @robpike.io
item.description:
Running MacOS 27.0.1. I usually wait for the .1 release but was trying unsuccessfully to resolve an issue.

I notice two small things.

1) There is a noticeable delay in waking up after fingerprint unlock, perhaps a full second. There was no detectable delay before.
2) Scrolling in Safari is jumpy now, quantized. Again, new behavior.

Wondering if others see this.

Please don't tell me to run some other OS or web browser, as I already do so in other contexts. I have my reasons to do what I do.

item.title: Writing some code today, a massive refactor to enable some…
item.dc:creator: @robpike.io
item.description:
Writing some code today, a massive refactor to enable some long-needed functionality, and just when I thought I was going to hit the wall and need a major detour to align huge disparate parts, it turned out an old abstraction fitted perfectly and the hardest problem was already solved. Pure joy. Euphoria.

And then I thought, if I had an LLM agent do this, there would be no joy. None for me, because I wouldn't have found it, and none for it, because LLMs are just automata.

I won today.

item.title: People constantly say they "can't do math" in their heads, when what…
item.dc:creator: @robpike.io
item.description:
People constantly say they "can't do math" in their heads, when what they really mean is "arithmetic". But "arithmetic" is harder to say than "math". So let's start calling arithmetic "rith", which is easy to say (and also sounds a bit like "rizz", which is fun).

Also, I _can_ do rith in my head, but I know that's nerdy and maybe you can't.
